title: Business email compromise and payment fraud against Fabrikam's own finance and HR
description: A spoofed, lookalike, or compromised mailbox persuades finance, payroll, or People staff to change bank details or release a payment, so Fabrikam money or employees' pay goes to an attacker. Day-1 conditions: Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 on default policies; the main domain's DMARC at p=none, with aggregate reports that go to a mailbox nobody reviews; of the two older brand domains, one no longer sends mail but publishes no SPF or DMARC record, and the other sends only through a marketing service and has no DMARC record; and push or SMS MFA (A-01, A-05). How bank changes are verified today is confirmed in discovery.
treatment: Mitigate: impersonation protection and DMARC enforcement; phishing-resistant MFA for payment approvers; separation of duties in finance roles; out-of-band verification of every bank-detail and payment change, including requests by voice or video call and requests summarized by an AI assistant (document 16, AIC-05 and AIC-06); finance and payroll training; detections, an MDR provider, and an executive tabletop

title: Ransomware or destructive attack on corporate endpoints and Microsoft 365 data
description: Ransomware affiliates get in through phishing, a stolen session, or an unpatched system, take data, then encrypt or delete corporate devices and Microsoft 365 content, stopping internal work and exposing sensitive company data kept in mail and OneDrive. Day-1 conditions: no endpoint detection and response on E3, no Microsoft 365 backup beyond retention settings, and alerts sent to a shared mailbox (A-06, A-07, A-09).
treatment: Mitigate: attack surface reduction, blocked legacy authentication, phishing-resistant MFA, and patching; endpoint detection and response with automatic attack disruption and an MDR provider (licensing per ADR-001); immutable Microsoft 365 backup with restore tests; one endpoint standard; sensitive data moved out of mailboxes
review_cadence: Monthly status at the IT and Security Steering Group; every Quarterly Risk Review; after each restore test and when MDR coverage starts

title: Former employees or contractors keep access after they leave
description: Offboarding runs on emails from People to IT and sometimes lags, with no access reviews (A-03), so a departed worker's accounts in Microsoft 365, SaaS, or internal tools can stay enabled. Most credible outcome: a late removal reported as a SOC 2 exception against CC6.2; less likely but worse: data misuse.
treatment: Mitigate: HR-driven joiner, mover, and leaver automation with an urgent leaver path (ADR-002); single sign-on and SCIM deprovisioning for SaaS; access reviews; a leaver checklist for systems outside the feed
review_cadence: Monthly status with KPI-12 at the IT and Security Steering Group; every Quarterly Risk Review; after any late leaver

title: Excessive, stale, or standing privileged access
description: Several standing Global Administrators using push or SMS MFA and no just-in-time access (A-01) mean one phished or socially engineered administrator could take over the whole Microsoft 365 tenant; product production access follows Engineering's own process.
treatment: Mitigate: emergency access accounts and MFA on every administrator in Phase 1; fewer than five Global Administrators and separate admin accounts; phishing-resistant MFA for administrators; Privileged Identity Management from Phase 4 (licensing per ADR-001); admin role reviews; admin sessions only from compliant workstations
review_cadence: Monthly with KPI-09 at the IT and Security Steering Group until it meets its target; every Quarterly Risk Review

title: Company and employee data exposed through oversharing in Microsoft 365, made worse by AI assistants
description: Anyone links, broad site permissions, and sensitive files kept in mail and OneDrive (A-06) let data reach people who should not see it; an AI assistant that searches everything a user can open makes such files easy to find.
treatment: Mitigate and avoid: Anyone links limited, then removed; manual sensitivity labels and DLP for payroll identifiers; site access review and interim protections before any Copilot pilot; AI rules and training; the AI security controls in document 16 (AIC-02, AIC-03, AIC-05, AIC-11)

title: Compromise of a corporate application or integration credential
description: A stolen API key or service principal secret, or a compromised connection between corporate SaaS applications, gives an attacker a trusted path that looks like authorized traffic; the acquisitions left duplicate and unmanaged connections (A-08).
treatment: Mitigate and transfer: an integration and application inventory with named owners; secret management and rotation; app consent and workload identity controls; third-party reviews and contract terms under POL-10
review_cadence: Monthly status at the IT and Security Steering Group; every Quarterly Risk Review; when an integration, partner, or credential owner changes

title: Unmanaged and duplicate SaaS left over from acquisitions
description: Duplicate tools, no application inventory, and partial single sign-on (A-08) leave data in applications nobody owns, miss offboarding, and carry vendor terms and spend nobody reviews.
treatment: Mitigate and avoid: application inventory and discovery; single sign-on and SCIM for the applications kept; duplicates retired with data export and deletion; vendor review under POL-10
review_cadence: Monthly status at the IT and Security Steering Group; every Quarterly Risk Review; at each consolidation milestone

title: Not enough logging or response capacity to investigate an incident within required notification timelines
description: Alerts go to a shared mailbox, nobody covers nights or weekends, and audit logging runs at standard retention (A-07), so Fabrikam may not be able to say what an attacker touched before the shortest required notification clock runs out.
treatment: Mitigate and share: an MDR provider for round-the-clock coverage (ADR-003); a log archive and at least one year of identity and Microsoft 365 audit history; a contract clause inventory that sets the planning clock; an incident response plan and exercises
review_cadence: Monthly status at the IT and Security Steering Group; every Quarterly Risk Review; after each SEV-1 or SEV-2 incident and each exercise; when the clause inventory changes the planning clock

title: A SOC 2 exception or a qualified opinion
description: Evidence gathered by hand near audit time, unclear control owners, and stale policies (A-10) risk exceptions or a qualified opinion that would undermine the report customers rely on.
treatment: Mitigate: protect the current review period (M4); named control owners and continuous evidence; a refreshed policy set; a compliance automation platform if ADR-007 approves one
review_cadence: Monthly status at the IT and Security Steering Group; every Quarterly Risk Review; at M4 (end of March 2027)

title: Privacy non-compliance for employee or workforce data under state law
description: Applicant and employee records and Fabrikam's own workforce data fall under state privacy and employee monitoring laws whose reach depends on facts General Counsel must confirm. A change to how employee data is collected, monitored, or retained that skipped privacy review could cross a legal line without anyone noticing.
treatment: Mitigate: privacy coordination and POL-15 retention; data inventories; only identity attributes leave the HR system; employee monitoring notices where required; privacy review before any change to how employee data is collected, monitored, or retained; the AI rules in POL-02 for AI applied to workforce data

title: Confidential data leaks through unsanctioned AI tools
description: Employees use public AI tools without guidance (A-12), so confidential company data, source code, or contracts can be pasted into services with no data protection commitments, kept by providers, or used to train models outside Fabrikam's control.
treatment: Mitigate: an approved enterprise AI tool with data protection commitments; AI rules in POL-02 by data classification; intake for new AI tools; training; DLP for Copilot and Copilot Chat prompts (preview, as of 2026-10-14); discovery of generative AI apps where licensed; consent limits and vendor terms (document 16: AIC-01, AIC-02, AIC-04, AIC-07)
review_cadence: Monthly status at the IT and Security Steering Group; every Quarterly Risk Review; at the Copilot pilot decision; when discovery shows new generative AI use

title: Key-person dependency in a small IT team
description: An IT Operations Manager and three IT generalists hold most of the know-how for Microsoft 365 administration, devices, and the service desk, with no dedicated security staff, so one absence or departure can stall changes or slow an incident response.
treatment: Mitigate and share: an MDR provider for after-hours detection; runbooks and a knowledge base; automation of routine work; cross-training and named deputies; contracted specialist help for surge and build work
review_cadence: Monthly status at the IT and Security Steering Group; every Quarterly Risk Review; after each joiner or leaver in the IT team

title: A fraudulent remote hire passes onboarding and receives credentials
description: Someone using a false or borrowed identity is hired into a remote role, passes onboarding, and receives working credentials and a laptop, then acts as an insider with legitimate access to Microsoft 365, SaaS, and, depending on the role, company data or source code. Day-1 conditions: onboarding runs on email requests from People to IT, accounts are created by hand, and first sign-in uses a password with push or SMS (A-01, A-03); how candidates' identities are checked during hiring is confirmed in discovery.
treatment: Mitigate: identity verification before first credentials are released (document 07); the joiner checklist; pre-hire screening under POL-14; birthright access limited to the role, with access reviews; sign-in and data access monitoring with the MDR provider
review_cadence: Monthly status at the IT and Security Steering Group; every Quarterly Risk Review; after any suspected fraudulent hire or failed identity check; when the onboarding steps in document 07 change
